answer.evidence: Rows 1-5 form a wood top band that brightens downward and ends in a light front-edge line at row 5 (L=180). Rows 6-7 are darker eave shadow (L=86, then L=45). This matches the green cabinet reference (top 5 + edge + eave). Below it is a front face of about 24 rows (rows 6-29) with three shelves of books and a plinth at rows 28-29. No side face is drawn. The shelf is a single body, so every major part has a top.

styleAnswer.evidence: Tile density is fine: 22 visible tones per tile against 17-20 for the stall and well, with 0% near-flat coverage. The weakness is structural. 100% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is a near-black line around the frame and shelf, where the stall, hedge and well use tinted dark-material tones (0-33% neutral). The wood frame and shelf boards read as about 3 steps (a light top edge, a mid tone and a dark line) with no grain or per-plank shading, and the book spines are mostly flat two-tone vertical bars. The colour variety is real, but it comes from the many different book colours rather than from shading depth within each material. Next to the stall and well references this looks cleaner and flatter, more like a sticker, and it is not at Beodeul's 5-6 steps per material.

surfaces.part: shelf face with book rows and shelf boards

answer.evidence: Rows 1-5 form a wood top band, lighter at rows 3-5, that ends in a light front-edge line at row 5. Rows 6-7 are dark eave shadow (#6e5032, then #3c281e). Below that is a front face about 22 rows tall (rows 8-29) with three shelf rows of books separated by shelf boards at rows 13-14 and 20-21, and a base at rows 28-29. This matches the green cabinet reference (top 5 + edge + eave). The top surface is 5 rows, not a 1-2 row rim.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 22 distinct colours in total, and the per-tile figure is also 22, so the whole piece is built from that one small set. Its density per tile (22 visible tones) is at or above the stall (17) and well (20), and it has 0% near-flat coverage. That richness comes mostly from the many book colours, which are narrow 2px vertical strips with little internal shading. The wood frame and shelf boards carry only about 3 lightness steps (a light top rail, a mid body and a dark edge), against roughly 5-6 steps on Beodeul's wood and roof ramps. The dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, unlike the stall (1%), the hedge (0%) and the well (33%), which have tinted outlines. So the frame reads as a uniform dark outline around the whole shape rather than a dark brown tone of the wood, which is the sticker look. The shelf interior is a regular grid of identical rows with no per-book highlights, grain or wear. The piece is clean and readable, but its shading and outline are shallower than the same-kind references, so it fails.
